findings.title: Backup-code login can bypass password verification with a dummy TOTP value
findings.body: The preceding password verification runs only when `credentials.totpCode` is empty, but the new backup-code branch takes precedence over TOTP verification whenever `backupCode` is supplied. A caller can therefore submit an email, a valid backup code, and any nonempty `totpCode` to sign in without knowing the password; the dummy TOTP is never validated. This turns a backup second factor into a standalone login credential. Ensure the password (or verified identity-provider authentication) is checked independently of which second factor is submitted.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
findings.body: Backup-code validation reads the encrypted code list and then unconditionally overwrites it using an update filtered only by user ID. Two concurrent login requests can read the same list, validate the same code, and both successfully authenticate. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's removals, making a consumed code usable again. Use an atomic compare-and-swap against the original stored value, or a transaction with appropriate locking, and reject or retry when another request has changed the list.
